what_its_for: Remdesivir is an antiviral medicine used to treat COVID-19 (coronavirus disease) in adults and children who are in the hospital or at high risk of getting very sick. It works by blocking the virus from making copies of itself inside your body, which helps slow down and stop the infection.
how_to_take: Remdesivir is given as an IV (intravenous) infusion directly into your vein through a needle. A nurse or healthcare provider will give you this medicine at a hospital, clinic, or infusion center. You will NOT give this medicine to yourself at home. Each infusion usually takes about 30 to 120 minutes. Stay seated or lying down during the infusion and let your nurse know right away if you feel any discomfort, dizziness, nausea, or unusual symptoms during or after the infusion.
dosing: For most adults and children weighing at least 40 kg (about 88 pounds), the usual dose is 200 mg on Day 1 (the first day), followed by 100 mg once daily on Days 2 and 3 for outpatients, or Days 2 through 5 (up to 10 days) for hospitalized patients depending on how sick you are. For smaller children, the dose is based on their weight. Your doctor will decide the right dose and number of days for you. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions.
missed_dose: Because this medicine is given by a healthcare provider in a clinic or hospital setting, you are unlikely to miss a dose on your own. However, if you miss or cannot make a scheduled appointment for your infusion, contact your doctor or healthcare team as soon as possible to reschedule. Do not try to make up a missed dose on your own. Finishing the full course of treatment is very important to help fight the infection.
storage: You do not need to store this medicine at home. Your healthcare provider or pharmacy will handle all storage. For reference, the liquid form (solution) must be kept refrigerated between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C) and must be used within a certain time after being prepared. The powder form is stored at room temperature. Always keep medicines out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking chloroquine or hydroxychloroquine at the same time as remdesivir, as these medicines can reduce how well remdesivir works. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL medicines, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are taking before starting remdesivir. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery if you feel dizzy, lightheaded, or unwell after your infusion. Follow your doctor's guidance on activity levels while you are being treated.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room right away if you experience any of the following: sudden drop in blood pressure, fast or irregular heartbeat, trouble breathing or shortness of breath, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, severe skin rash or itching, nausea or vomiting that is severe, unusual bruising or bleeding, dark or tea-colored urine, yellowing of your skin or eyes (signs of liver problems), or any other sudden or severe symptoms. Also tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, as your doctor may need to adjust your treatment.
when_it_works: Remdesivir starts working in your body right away after the first infusion, but you may not feel better immediately. Most people begin to notice improvement within a few days of starting treatment. It is very important to complete all of your scheduled infusions even if you start feeling better, because stopping early could allow the virus to come back or get worse. Remdesivir works best when started as early as possible after your COVID-19 diagnosis.
special_populations: Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Talk to your doctor about the risks and benefits before using remdesivir. It has been used in pregnancy when the benefits outweigh the risks, but always consult your healthcare provider. Children: Remdesivir can be used in children who weigh at least 3.5 kg (about 7.7 pounds) and meet certain criteria; the dose is adjusted by weight. Elderly patients: No special dose adjustment is needed based on age alone, but your doctor will monitor your kidney and liver function. Kidney or liver disease: Remdesivir may not be recommended if you have severe kidney or liver problems. Your doctor will check your lab values before and during treatment to make sure it is safe for you.
